newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertain direction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertain direction.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Thursday on uncertain short-term direction, traders said.
The key December 1996 contract ended at an intra-day high of 21,240 yuan ($2,557) per tonne, rising 60 yuan. It opened at a low of 20,980.
September rose 20 to 21,400 yuan. October dropped 40 to 21,250 and November 20 to 21,130. The January 1997 contract rose 20 to 21,200. March was unchanged at 21,200 and April fell 10 to 21,190.
Combined volume fell to 39,090 tonnes from 57,710.
Copper opened down on overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, but short-covering pushed prices up for most of the session.
Traders said that long and short position holders were mixed on the short-term direction, which triggered active trading at low levels, but neither came out the winner.
"Many investors stayed on the sidelines on the unclear market trend but there were speculators buying and selling for quick profit," one trader said.
Traders said copper would be supported at 21,000 yuan in the short term but that it will meet heavy selling by industrial users because of an over-supply of spot copper.
Analysts expect copper to continue moving between 21,000 and 21,500 over the next few days.
Aluminium ended mixed in slow trading. September fell 30 to 14,340 yuan and October did not trade. November rose 50 to 14,400. Combined volume fell to 240 tonnes from 410.
